title: Your apps can now open in Claude, and Claude can work in them
summary: Partner apps can now open inside Claude beside the chat or full screen, and Claude can edit the live page, row, or file, with the user approving actions as they would for any connector. Tools can be pinned to the sidebar and opened from the + menu without a prompt, rolling out on web and desktop for all plans starting with Asana, Canva, Notion, and Atlassian. Developers can build full apps on the MCP Apps standard, which is in public preview.

title: Linked billing on the Claude Platform
summary: In beta, third-party tools can let customers pay for Claude API usage without sharing an API key. Customers link their org through Anthropic's hosted flow, approve each platform, and set monthly spend limits, with Anthropic handling billing and approvals. Requests run in the platform's org, so customer IP allowlists, encryption keys, and retention settings do not apply.

title: Introducing Claude Meetings
summary: Claude joins video calls as a visible participant and starts work during the meeting, answering questions aloud or in chat, building docs and whiteboards live, and writing notes and action items on a claude.ai meeting page. It is in beta on Team and Enterprise with Google Meet supported and other platforms coming soon. It saves transcripts, summaries, and screen descriptions but not audio, and it is not available with zero data retention, HIPAA-ready configs, or customer-managed keys.

title: Operate Claude Managed Agents inside your security perimeter
summary: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents are in private beta, and the harness, sandboxes, credentials, and session history now all run in the customer's environment instead of only the sandbox. Model routing can go direct to Anthropic, Bedrock, Google Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, or a customer's own gateway. Reasoning is separated from code execution, credentials are kept out of the sandbox, network allowlists apply, and session logs are exported via OpenTelemetry; access is through an Anthropic account team.

title: The Claude Tag guide for startups
summary: This guide covers Claude Tag (beta), which lets Team and Enterprise teams @mention Claude in Slack, and shares setups from eight startups, including on-call triage, Slack threads to draft PRs, internal Q&A, and recurring reports. Campfire went from mention to open PR in 21 minutes, and Moritz cut a daily update from about an hour to 5 minutes. Guardrails include draft PRs only with human review, scoped access, spend limits, and security review, and the advice is to start with one clear task in an existing channel.

title: Using Claude Opus 5.5 as your daily driver for knowledge work
summary: This guide recommends Opus 5.5 for research, analysis, memos, spreadsheets, and decks, and Opus 5.5 is now the default on Pro, Max, Ultra, and Team plans. Pricing is $4/$20 per million tokens versus $2/$10 for Sonnet 5.5, and a financial modeling task took 63 minutes versus 93 for Opus 5 at half the cost, with Medium effort matching or beating Opus 5 at High. Tips include asking for finished files, connecting work files, and stating the goal and output up front.
